options.text: Post-LN is LayerNorm(x + S(x)), while Pre-LN is x + S(LayerNorm(x)); Pre-LN moves normalization onto the sublayer input while retaining an unnormalized identity path.
options.rationale: The two canonical variants place LayerNorm outside versus inside the residual block, so they are different forward compositions even with identical S parameters.

questions.stem: One attention head has value vectors v1 = u, v2 = u, and v3 = 0. Query A assigns weights [0.9, 0.0, 0.1], while query B assigns [0.0, 0.9, 0.1]. Ignoring output projection, what can be concluded from the two head outputs?

options.text: The weight vectors are actually equal because fixed value vectors determine the compatibility distribution for both queries.
options.rationale: Queries and keys determine the stated weights; duplicated values can make different weight vectors produce the same routed result.

options.text: The outputs cannot be computed without the key vectors because attention combines keys rather than values after softmax.
options.rationale: The weights are already given, and the post-softmax mixture uses the value vectors rather than the keys.

options.text: Both outputs equal u because softmax attention keeps only each query's largest-weight source and discards the 0.1 contribution.
options.rationale: Softmax attention retains every nonzero coefficient, so the zero-valued third position reduces each mixture to 0.9u.

options.text: Both outputs equal 0.9u; duplicated payloads make the output insufficient to identify which of the first two positions received the weight.
options.rationale: Each weighted sum is 0.9u plus 0.1 times zero, despite the two queries addressing different source positions.

provenance.derivation: For query A the output is 0.9u + 0.0u + 0.1(0) = 0.9u; query B gives 0.0u + 0.9u + 0.1(0) = 0.9u. The equal outputs do not identify which duplicated value position carried the mass.
provenance.independence_note: The keyed operation reasons backward from equal outputs under duplicated payloads. It is not a forward two-value mixture, a value-projection ablation, a single-value perturbation, or a cross-attention shape audit.

questions.stem: During teacher-forced training, the attention logits for shifted-decoder query position i = 1 are [0, 0, 100] for key positions j = 0, 1, 2. Which implementation produces the standard causal attention probabilities for this row?

options.text: Apply softmax to all three logits during training and defer the causal mask until generated tokens replace teacher-forced inputs.
options.rationale: The future token at j = 2 is already present during teacher forcing and would dominate the unmasked distribution.

options.text: Set logits for j greater than or equal to i to negative infinity before softmax, producing probabilities [1, 0, 0].
options.rationale: Standard shifted-decoder visibility includes j = i; only positions strictly to the right are excluded.

options.text: Evaluate each training row serially without changing its logits, because sequential execution itself prevents the future key from contributing.
options.rationale: Execution order does not remove a supplied logit's softmax contribution; the forbidden edge must be masked explicitly.

options.text: Set the j = 2 logit to negative infinity before softmax, producing probabilities [0.5, 0.5, 0] in the parallel matrix operation.
options.rationale: Causal masking removes the future logit before normalization while retaining both permitted positions and parallel row evaluation.

provenance.derivation: For query i = 1, the inclusive causal rule permits j = 0 and j = 1 and excludes j = 2. Replacing the future logit with negative infinity before softmax leaves equal permitted logits and therefore probabilities [0.5, 0.5, 0].
provenance.independence_note: The keyed operation audits the numerical masking stage and renormalized probabilities. It is not merely choosing an edge inequality, distinguishing training from generation, constructing a packed-sequence mask, or tracing a future activation path.

questions.stem: A deterministic decoder evaluates the same fixed token prefix in two ways: one teacher-forced full-sequence pass with the standard causal mask, and one token-at-a-time pass that reuses exact cached keys and values. Parameters, positions, and arithmetic are otherwise identical. Before sampling, how should the per-position outputs compare?

options.text: The full pass may use unrestricted attention because the future-information boundary begins with incremental generation, so its outputs can differ.
options.rationale: Teacher forcing contains future inputs and therefore needs the same causal boundary to match autoregressive decoding.

options.text: The incremental pass excludes its current shifted-input position, while the full causal pass includes that diagonal position, so they differ systematically.
options.rationale: Both executions permit the current shifted-input position and exclude positions to its right.

options.text: The outputs match after the teacher-forced rows are evaluated serially, because parallel matrix evaluation changes which causal dependencies exist.
options.rationale: A parallel masked matrix and serial incremental queries implement the same permitted edges; scheduling does not add dependencies.

options.text: Corresponding outputs match up to numerical effects because each query sees the same permitted shifted-input prefix in both executions.
options.rationale: Causal full-sequence evaluation and exact cached evaluation differ in scheduling and reused intermediates, not in the visible keys and values.

provenance.source_scope: Vaswani et al. ground shifted decoder inputs and causal masking. Shazeer grounds exact incremental decoding with retained key-value state. The equivalence follows by matching the permitted prefix at each query position.
provenance.independence_note: The keyed operation compares two execution schedules by their visible key-value sets. It is not selecting a mask inequality, normalizing one masked logit row, testing suffix invariance, or inventorying cached tensors.

questions.stem: An encoder-decoder Transformer is trained with the complete source sequence and a shifted target sequence. There is no source or target padding. Which visibility pattern preserves autoregressive target prediction while retaining access to the encoded source?

options.text: Leave target self-attention unrestricted because encoder-decoder Transformer blocks stay bidirectional by architecture when a causal mask is configured.
options.rationale: The decoder's configured self-attention mask controls target-side information flow; the architecture label does not override blocked future edges.

options.text: Use a strict target self-attention mask that excludes the aligned shifted-input position, while cross-attention reads the encoded source.
options.rationale: The standard shifted-target alignment permits the diagonal target input; causality excludes positions to its right.

options.text: Run the target rows serially because exposing the encoded source through cross-attention prevents a parallel causal training computation.
options.rationale: Masked target self-attention and source cross-attention can both be evaluated for the teacher-forced target rows in parallel.

options.text: Use inclusive causal target self-attention, let each target query inspect the complete nonpadding encoder sequence, and compute target rows in parallel.
options.rationale: Causality constrains target-to-target edges; decoder cross-attention may condition each target position on the fully encoded source.

provenance.source_scope: Vaswani et al. specify masked decoder self-attention over shifted targets and a separate decoder attention sublayer over encoder outputs. The no-padding condition isolates those two visibility contracts.
provenance.independence_note: The keyed operation assigns different visibility rules to decoder self-attention and encoder cross-attention. It is not computing one triangular row, comparing full and cached execution, composing packed-example masks, or deriving query-key-value shapes.

questions.stem: During one teacher-forced layer pass of an offline encoder-decoder Transformer, the complete nonpadding source has been encoded into cross-attention key-value positions s0, s1, s2. The right-shifted decoder input supplies self-attention key-value positions t0, t1, t2, with no target padding. For decoder query row i = 1, which key sets are visible?

options.text: Target self-attention sees {t0, t1, t2}; source cross-attention sees {s0, s1, s2}.
options.rationale: Teacher forcing makes t2 available in the input tensor, so the training mask must already prevent row i = 1 from reading that future target position.

options.text: Target self-attention sees {t0, t1}; source cross-attention sees {s0, s1, s2}.
options.rationale: Inclusive causal self-attention admits the right-shifted decoder prefix through i, while cross-attention may use every position in the fully encoded nonpadding source.

options.text: Target self-attention sees {t0}; source cross-attention sees {s0, s1, s2}.
options.rationale: Because t1 is a right-shifted decoder input rather than the label predicted at row i = 1, the inclusive causal rule permits it and hides only positions to its right.

options.text: Target self-attention sees {t0, t1}; source cross-attention sees {s0, s1}.
options.rationale: The target index defines the decoder self-attention boundary, not a prefix boundary on the already encoded source; no source padding or streaming mask removes s2 here.

provenance.source_scope: Vaswani et al. sections 3.1 and 3.2 specify right-shifted decoder inputs, masking of subsequent target positions, and a separate encoder-decoder attention sublayer in which decoder positions attend over encoder outputs. The indexed no-padding scenario and distractor wording are original synthesis.
provenance.revision_reason: The parent asks for the visibility rule abstractly; this revision forces an exact indexed self-attention and cross-attention trace and directly diagnoses transfer of the target causal triangle onto full encoder memory.
provenance.independence_note: This immutable wording revision deliberately retains family f_causal_cross_attention_mask_scope and must not count as independent evidence from q_causal_cross_attention_mask_scope_001. The keyed operation enumerates exact target-self and source-cross key sets at one decoder row and distinguishes the target causal boundary from full-source visibility.

questions.stem: With parameters fixed, an engineer perturbs the input representation at one position r in a Transformer encoder layer and observes a changed output at another position s. The layer has unrestricted self-attention, a position-wise feed-forward sublayer, and residual paths. Which explanation identifies a possible cross-position path without claiming the change is guaranteed?

options.text: The feed-forward sublayer at s reads row r directly and mixes it into s even when self-attention contributes no route between them.
options.rationale: The feed-forward map is applied separately to each position and cannot directly read a different sequence row.

options.text: The perturbation can alter r's key or value, attention at s can route that difference, and later position-wise transformations process the changed state locally.
options.rationale: Self-attention supplies the cross-position edge; its learned score and projected content determine whether the particular intervention changes s.

options.text: The observation conflicts with the residual identity path, which restores the original state at s and erases any attention-branch update.
options.rationale: A residual adds the branch output to the prior state; it does not cancel an attention-mediated change by definition.

options.text: The observation proves Transformers are inherently bidirectional, so the same r-to-s route would remain available even under a mask that blocks that direction.
options.rationale: This encoder layer permits the route because its self-attention is unrestricted; a configured mask can remove it, so the architecture name does not fix visibility.

provenance.source_scope: Vaswani et al. ground the token-to-token path in self-attention, the per-position feed-forward map, and residual addition. The intervention and observed change are stipulated original scenario evidence.
provenance.independence_note: The keyed operation localizes an observed cross-position intervention effect. It is not removing attention, ablating encoder-decoder cross-attention, assigning cross-attention tensor roles, or comparing sublayer order.

questions.stem: A service using standard dense full self-attention keeps one checkpoint resident. A long request exhausts temporary memory, but after the request is released the process returns to the same model-memory baseline and serves a short request without reloading weights. Monitoring shows that the checkpoint hash and learned tensor shapes never change. Which diagnosis best fits?

options.text: The failure is in request-local activation or workspace capacity; longer inputs increase dense pairwise attention work without adding learned parameters.
options.rationale: The stable model-memory baseline and unchanged checkpoint identify fixed parameters, while the request lifecycle localizes the exhausted memory to input-dependent runtime state.

options.text: The long request adds work in direct proportion to token count, because full attention forms one query-key score for each input token.
options.rationale: Full attention forms a score for each permitted query-key pair, so its request-scoped work is not limited to one score per token.

options.text: The service temporarily creates learned token-specific parameter rows for the long request and discards them when the request ends.
options.rationale: Applying fixed learned tensors at more positions creates additional activations, not hidden token-specific parameters.

options.text: The inference failure is unrelated to pairwise attention, because its quadratic cost is a training artifact caused by retained gradients.
options.rationale: Inference removes gradient storage but still performs the forward query-key interactions required by full attention.

provenance.source_scope: Vaswani et al. support shared learned projection tensors and dense pairwise self-attention over an input sequence; Goodfellow et al. support the distinction between learned parameters and input-dependent computation. The request lifecycle, checkpoint hash, learned tensor shapes, and memory observations are stipulated original scenario facts; the keyed diagnosis is the authored inference being tested. Neither source validates this service or the authored difficulty.
provenance.independence_note: This item intentionally reuses f_transformer_sequence_shape_audit because it requires the same fixed-parameters-versus-input-dependent-runtime-resources inference as q_transformer_sequence_shape_audit_001. It is an easier operational presentation, not an independent evidence opportunity, and responses to the two items must not be counted as separate-family verification.

questions.stem: In deterministic evaluation, a test sets one standard Transformer encoder layer's self-attention branch output to zero before its residual addition. The position-wise feed-forward map, per-token normalization, and residual additions remain. Two runs differ in the first input token while holding the second input token fixed, yet the second token's output also differs. Which diagnosis matches the specified layer?

options.text: A position-wise feed-forward map reads all token rows and can transmit the first-token change to the second row.
options.rationale: A position-wise feed-forward map applies the same feature transformation separately to each token row.

options.text: An unlisted cross-token dependency or implementation fault is present; each specified remaining operation acts separately on the second position.
options.rationale: With the attention contribution clamped away, the listed feed-forward, normalization, and residual operations cannot transmit the first token's intervention to the second.

options.text: Residual connections make the order and presence of attention and feed-forward sublayers irrelevant, so the feed-forward branch substitutes for the zeroed attention route.
options.rationale: A residual addition preserves information already present at a position; it does not create a route from a different token row.

options.text: Calling the layer an encoder preserves a bidirectional route after its listed sequence-mixing attention branch is disabled.
options.rationale: Directionality follows enabled information paths; the architecture label cannot restore a disabled cross-token contribution.

provenance.source_scope: Vaswani et al. support self-attention as the sequence-interaction path, position-wise feed-forward processing, residual addition, and LayerNorm within Transformer layers. Deterministic evaluation, the branch intervention, the per-token normalization boundary, and the observed output change are stipulated original test facts; the keyed fault diagnosis is the authored inference being tested. The paper does not validate this implementation or item.
provenance.independence_note: This item intentionally reuses f_transformer_axis_mixing because it is the diagnostic inversion of q_transformer_token_mixing_001: both require recognizing that the listed position-wise and residual paths cannot replace disabled attention as a cross-token route. It is an easier test surface, not an independent evidence opportunity, and the two responses must remain family-collapsed.

questions.stem: With a nonempty previous cache, an incremental multi-query self-attention kernel updates one layer with K = concat(previous K, current k, time) but V = concat(current v, previous V, time). It then computes a = softmax(q times K-transpose) and y = aV. All tensor shapes and sequence lengths pass validation. Which diagnosis is correct?

options.text: Caching the previous queries beside K and V repairs the mismatch because old queries recover which value row belongs to each key coefficient.
options.rationale: Earlier queries are not the missing association. The cache must keep each key row aligned with its corresponding value row.

options.text: The mismatch is expected because multi-query attention shares queries rather than keys and values; sharing Q would make the opposing K/V orders equivalent.
options.rationale: Multi-query attention keeps multiple query heads and shares K/V heads; neither form of head sharing permits independently reordered K and V time rows.

options.text: The kernel misaligns positions: a coefficient derived from one key can multiply another position's value, so K and V need the same temporal ordering.
options.rationale: Incremental attention preserves aligned key-value pairs. Appending K while prepending V reverses only one history and changes the weighted value routing despite valid shapes.

options.text: The kernel is exact because sharing K/V heads collapses prefix positions into an unordered summary, making prepend and append equivalent.
options.rationale: Head sharing does not remove the time axis. Distinct prefix positions and their aligned key-value pairs remain semantically ordered.

provenance.source_scope: Vaswani et al. section 3.2.1 defines attention as key-derived softmax weights multiplied by the aligned value matrix. Shazeer section 2.4 appends new K and V entries along the same incremental memory axis before applying that contraction. The opposite-order mutation and fault-localization task are stipulated original code-review facts.
provenance.independence_note: The keyed operation diagnoses a shape-valid cache corruption by tracing positional K-V alignment through incremental code. It is not a multi-query head-axis inventory, a retain-K/V versus discard-Q statement, an asymptotic complexity comparison, or a cached-query masking question.

questions.stem: A frozen multi-query decoder processes the same prefix through the first cache eviction. Exact implementation E retains every prior key and value, its causal mask permits every prior position including those W evicts, and it matches full-prefix masked logits. Windowed implementation W keeps only the newest 1,024 key-value positions. At this step E and W choose the same greedy next token, but their full logit vectors have not been compared. Which audit conclusion is warranted?

options.text: W becomes exact if it retains the evicted positions' past queries, because those queries reconstruct the missing keys and values at the next step.
options.rationale: Past queries are not reusable prefix memory and cannot recreate key-value entries that W removed from the visible attention set.

options.text: W remains exact because multi-query attention shares query heads, so key-value positions older than the window have no effect on future logits.
options.rationale: Multi-query attention keeps multiple query heads and shares key-value heads; it does not make older retained positions irrelevant.

options.text: W remains exact because sharing key-value heads collapses the time history into its newest entry, and the matching top token confirms equivalence.
options.rationale: Head sharing preserves distinct time entries, and one matching argmax does not establish equality of the full logit vectors.

options.text: W bounded memory by changing the visible context; a matching argmax establishes neither logit equality nor future generated-trajectory equivalence, so W needs separate quality and resource evaluation.
options.rationale: Eviction removes key-value positions available to E, so one coincident selected token is insufficient evidence of equal distributions or later generated behavior.

provenance.source_scope: Shazeer's sections 2.4 and 3 define exact incremental multi-query attention with a distinct retained K/V entry for every prior position while removing only the K/V head axis. Vaswani et al. equation 1 makes the head output depend on the visible key-value set. The 1,024-position window, unobserved full-logit comparison, and matching argmax are stipulated original audit facts; no empirical safety claim is attributed to either paper.
provenance.independence_note: The keyed counterfactual distinguishes exact full-history reuse from bounded eviction when one observed greedy action matches but distributional equivalence is untested. It is not a no-cache asymptotic comparison, multi-query tensor inventory, append/discard state transition, K/V ordering fault, or causal-mask question.

questions.stem: One attention head has value vectors v1 = u, v2 = u, and v3 = w, with w different from u. Two possible attention rows are A = [0.8, 0.1, 0.1] and B = [0.1, 0.8, 0.1]. An audit retained only the pre-output head result. Which conclusion follows?

options.text: The two rows are incompatible with the same values because the value vectors determine the compatibility distribution.
options.rationale: Queries and keys determine an attention row; duplicated values can let different rows produce the same routed result.

options.text: Neither result can be computed without the keys because attention combines keys rather than the stated values after softmax.
options.rationale: The rows are already supplied, and their coefficients multiply the stated value vectors.

options.text: Both results are u because softmax keeps the largest-weight source and discards each 0.1 contribution.
options.rationale: Ordinary softmax attention keeps every positive coefficient, including the contribution from w.

options.text: Both results are 0.9u + 0.1w, so the retained output is insufficient to identify whether attention row A or B occurred.
options.rationale: A yields 0.8u + 0.1u + 0.1w and B yields 0.1u + 0.8u + 0.1w; the duplicated payload makes those results equal.

provenance.source_scope: Vaswani et al. equation 1 defines the weighted value contraction. Brunner et al. section 3 establishes that attention weights need not be identifiable from a head output. The positive attention rows, duplicated-value witness, and retained-output audit are original algebraic synthesis rather than a quoted empirical result.
provenance.revision_reason: The parent used exact zero coefficients without stating a mask, which ordinary finite-logit softmax cannot produce. This immutable revision uses strictly positive normalized rows and makes the inverse retained-output inference explicit.
provenance.independence_note: This revision deliberately retains the parent's family and cannot count independently from q_attention_duplicate_value_identifiability_001. The family reasons inversely from a retained output to non-identifiability under duplicate values; it is not a forward value perturbation or value-projection ablation.

questions.stem: An autograd audit freezes queries and keys for two output rows, so A = [[0.6, 0.4], [0.2, 0.8]] and Y = AV. If upstream gradients at the output rows are g1 and g2, which gradients reach source values v1 and v2 through this weighted-sum path?

options.text: v1 receives 0.6g1 + 0.2g2 and v2 receives 0.4g1 + 0.8g2, which is the A-transpose times upstream-gradient trace.
options.rationale: Each source value contributes to both output rows, so reverse-mode accumulation sends every row's upstream gradient back through that value's attention coefficient.

options.text: No fixed-coefficient result exists because differentiating the values necessarily changes the attention matrix A.
options.rationale: The audit freezes queries and keys, so A is fixed with respect to the value path being differentiated.

options.text: Both value gradients are zero; the aligned key vectors receive A-transpose times the upstream gradients as the output payloads.
options.rationale: The forward contraction multiplies A by V, so this path sends the adjoint into the values rather than substituting keys as payloads.

options.text: v1 receives g1 and v2 receives g2 because each output routes gradient through its largest attention coefficient.
options.rationale: Softmax attention is a weighted sum, so every nonzero coefficient contributes to reverse-mode gradient routing.

provenance.source_scope: Vaswani et al. equation 1 supplies the Y = AV value-routing map, and Goodfellow et al. chapter 6 supplies reverse-mode differentiation through computational graphs. The fixed matrix, upstream vectors, and A-transpose derivation are original audit conditions.
provenance.derivation: Writing upstream rows as G = [g1; g2], the differential dY = A dV gives dL = trace(G-transpose A dV) = trace((A-transpose G)-transpose dV), hence dL/dV = A-transpose G.
provenance.independence_note: The keyed operation traces the adjoint A-transpose G from multiple output rows back into source values. It is not the released forward AV perturbation/projection operation and not the inverse duplicate-value identifiability family. Semantic independence still requires human review and later response evidence.
